findings.location: Paragraph: "In reckless abandonment he stepped off her deck …and a miracle happened." (English source paragraph about Peter stepping off the deck)
findings.source_quote: In reckless abandonment he stepped off her deck …and a miracle happened.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a Norwegian phrase that better captures the English sense of "reckless abandonment". Suggested wording: "I hensynsløs overgivelse steg han av dekket…" or "I vill overgivelse steg han av dekket…". Preserve the surrounding HTML and punctuation.
findings.translation_quote: I ukrenkelig overgivelse steg han av dekket …og et mirakel skjedde.

findings.location: Paragraph: "You do not need to go into foreign missions to experience the power of God released in your life."
findings.source_quote: You do not need to go into foreign missions to experience the power of God released in your life.
findings.suggested_fix: The translation "dra til utlendighet" is understandable but slightly awkward in contemporary Bokmål. Suggest: "Du trenger ikke å dra til utlandet for å erfare Guds kraft i ditt liv." Or, to keep the explicit mission context: "Du trenger ikke å dra til utlandet for misjonsarbeid for å erfare Guds kraft i ditt liv."
findings.translation_quote: Du trenger ikke å dra til utlendighet for å erfare Guds utløste kraft i ditt liv.

findings.location: Paragraph: "He had drawn many a draught of fish over her gunwales."
findings.source_quote: He had drawn many a draught of fish over her gunwales.
findings.suggested_fix: The phrase is slightly literal in Norwegian. Consider: "Han hadde dradd mange fiskelass over relingen" or "Han hadde dradd mange fangster over rekka." These are more idiomatic while preserving meaning.
findings.translation_quote: Han hadde dradd mange fiskelaster over hennes rekker.
